import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Prepare the data for visualization
# Group by 'KreisLang' and count the number of dogs
dogs_per_district = df.groupby('KreisLang')['AnzHunde'].sum().reset_index()

# Sort the values for better visualization
dogs_per_district = dogs_per_district.sort_values(by='AnzHunde', ascending=False)

# Set the style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a bar plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.barplot(data=dogs_per_district, x='AnzHunde', y='KreisLang', palette='Blues_d')

# Add titles and labels
plt.title('Number of Registered Dogs by District in Zurich', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('District', fontsize=14)

# Save the figure

```python
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Prepare the data for visualization
# Group by 'KreisLang' and count the number of dogs
dogs_per_district = df.groupby('KreisLang')['AnzHunde'].sum().reset_index()

# Sort the values for better visualization
dogs_per_district = dogs_per_district.sort_values(by='AnzHunde', ascending=False)

# Set the style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a bar plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.barplot(data=dogs_per_district, x='AnzHunde', y='KreisLang', palette='Blues_d')

# Add titles and labels
plt.title('Number of Registered Dogs by District in Zurich', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('District', fontsize=14)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
```
